title: Earned Value Analysis (EVA) Exam Review Quiz
subtitle: Concept-focused multiple-choice questions for project management review

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Earned Value Analysis (EVA)?
options: To integrate scope, schedule, and cost for objective project performance assessment
To replace all project schedules with budgets
To estimate team member productivity only
questions.explanation: EVA integrates scope, schedule, and cost to assess performance objectively.

questions.question: Which three metrics form the foundation of EVA calculations?
questions.explanation: Planned Value, Earned Value, and Actual Cost are the core input metrics.

questions.question: What does Planned Value (PV) represent?
options: The budgeted value of work that should have been completed by now
The value of completed work based on actual cost
questions.explanation: PV is the budgeted amount of work that was planned to be complete at a point in time.

questions.question: What is another name for Planned Value (PV)?
questions.explanation: PV is also known as BCWS.

questions.question: What does Earned Value (EV) measure?
options: Budgeted value of the work actually completed
Work planned to be completed next month
questions.explanation: EV measures the budgeted value of completed work.

questions.question: What is another name for Earned Value (EV)?
questions.explanation: EV is also known as BCWP.

questions.question: What does Actual Cost (AC) represent?
options: The real money spent on work completed so far
questions.explanation: AC is the actual cost incurred to date.

questions.question: What is another name for Actual Cost (AC)?
questions.explanation: AC is also called ACWP.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Schedule Variance (SV)?
questions.explanation: Schedule Variance is EV minus PV.

questions.question: What does a positive Schedule Variance (SV) indicate?
questions.explanation: A positive SV means more work was earned than planned, so the project is ahead of schedule.

questions.question: What does a negative Schedule Variance (SV) indicate?
questions.explanation: A negative SV means less work was earned than planned.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Schedule Performance Index (SPI)?
questions.explanation: SPI is EV divided by PV.

questions.question: What does SPI greater than 1 mean?
questions.explanation: SPI above 1 indicates schedule efficiency better than planned.

questions.question: What does SPI equal to 1 mean?
questions.explanation: SPI = 1 indicates the project is on schedule.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Cost Variance (CV)?
questions.explanation: Cost Variance is EV minus AC.

questions.question: What does a positive Cost Variance (CV) indicate?
questions.explanation: A positive CV means earned value exceeds actual cost, so the project is under budget.

questions.question: What does a negative Cost Variance (CV) indicate?
questions.explanation: A negative CV means the project has spent more than the value earned.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates Cost Performance Index (CPI)?
questions.explanation: CPI is Earned Value divided by Actual Cost.

questions.question: What does CPI greater than 1 mean?
questions.explanation: A CPI above 1 indicates cost efficiency better than planned.

questions.question: What does CPI less than 1 mean?
questions.explanation: A CPI below 1 indicates the project is spending more than the value earned.

questions.question: What does Budget at Completion (BAC) represent?
options: The budgeted value of scheduled work
questions.explanation: BAC is the total overall project budget.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Estimate at Completion (EAC)?
options: The expected final project cost based on current information
The value of work planned this week
The amount needed to stay on schedule
questions.explanation: EAC forecasts the total cost of the project at completion.

questions.question: Which formula is a valid method for calculating EAC when current cost variance is expected to continue?
questions.explanation: BAC divided by CPI is used when current cost performance is expected to continue.

questions.question: Which formula is used when current variances are not expected to continue?
questions.explanation: If variance is atypical and not expected to continue, use AC plus remaining planned work.

questions.question: Which EAC formula incorporates both schedule and cost performance?
questions.explanation: This hybrid formula uses both SPI and CPI to reflect combined performance.

questions.question: What does Estimate to Complete (ETC) represent?
options: The remaining money needed to finish the project
The amount of work ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: ETC is the cost required to complete the remaining work.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates ETC?
questions.explanation: ETC equals EAC minus AC.

questions.question: What does Variance at Completion (VAC) measure?
options: How much work is ahead of schedule
The forecasted cost difference at project completion
questions.explanation: VAC shows expected surplus or deficit at completion.

questions.question: Which formula correctly calculates VAC?
questions.explanation: VAC is BAC minus EAC.

questions.question: What does a positive VAC indicate?
questions.explanation: A positive VAC means the project should finish under budget.

questions.question: What does a negative VAC indicate?
questions.explanation: A negative VAC means the project is forecasted to exceed budget.

questions.question: What does TCPI stand for?
questions.explanation: TCPI stands for To Complete Performance Index.

questions.question: Which formula is used to calculate TCPI when the original budget is fixed?
questions.explanation: This formula shows the CPI required to finish on the original budget.

questions.question: What does TCPI greater than 1 imply?
options: Future efficiency must improve to meet budget
The project is already under budget at completion
The project is ahead of schedule
There is no need for control
questions.explanation: TCPI above 1 means the remaining work must be performed more efficiently than before.

questions.question: Which of the following is an absolute variance metric?
questions.explanation: SV is an absolute dollar variance metric.

questions.question: Which of the following is a relative index metric?
questions.explanation: SPI is a ratio-based efficiency index.

questions.question: Why are index metrics often better for comparing multiple projects?
options: They use the same dollar budget for all projects
They normalize performance as a ratio or percentage
They eliminate the need for EV
questions.explanation: Indices normalize performance, making projects with different sizes comparable.

questions.question: What is the main difference between variance metrics and index metrics?
options: Variance metrics are ratios; index metrics are dollars
Variance metrics show dollar magnitude; index metrics show relative efficiency
Variance metrics are only for cost; index metrics are only for schedule
Variance metrics require BAC; index metrics do not
questions.explanation: Variances show magnitude in dollars, while indices show performance ratios.

questions.question: Which statement about schedule and cost performance is correct?
options: A project cannot be ahead of schedule and over budget at the same time
Schedule and cost performance are always identical
A project can be ahead of schedule but over budget
If CPI is above 1, SPI must also be above 1
questions.explanation: Schedule and cost performance are independent and can diverge.

questions.question: What does SV compare?
questions.explanation: SV compares earned value to planned value.

questions.question: What does CV compare?
questions.explanation: CV compares earned value to actual cost.

questions.question: If EV is greater than PV, what does that imply?
options: The project is ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: EV above PV means more work has been earned than planned.

questions.question: If EV is less than AC, what does that imply?
questions.explanation: When earned value is less than actual cost, the project is over budget.

questions.question: Which metric answers the question: 'How much work should have been completed by now?'
questions.explanation: PV represents work that should have been completed at the status date.

questions.question: Which metric answers the question: 'How much work has actually been completed?'
questions.explanation: EV is the budgeted value of work actually completed.

questions.question: Which metric answers the question: 'How much money has actually been spent?'
questions.explanation: AC is the actual spending to date.

questions.question: Which project status is indicated by SV > 0 and CV > 0?
options: Ahead of schedule and under budget
Ahead of schedule and over budget
questions.explanation: Positive SV and CV indicate the project is ahead and under budget.

questions.question: Which project status is indicated by SV > 0 and CV < 0?
options: Ahead of schedule but over budget
questions.explanation: Positive schedule variance and negative cost variance indicate mixed performance.

questions.question: Which project status is indicated by SV < 0 and CV > 0?
options: Ahead of schedule and over budget
Ahead of schedule and under budget
questions.explanation: Negative SV and positive CV means the project is late but spending less than planned.

questions.question: Which project status is indicated by SV < 0 and CV < 0?
options: Ahead of schedule and under budget
Ahead of schedule and over budget
questions.explanation: Negative schedule and cost variances indicate poor performance on both dimensions.

questions.question: Which statement best describes EAC when current cost inefficiency is expected to persist?
questions.explanation: BAC divided by CPI projects final cost assuming current inefficiency continues.

questions.question: When would EAC = AC + (BAC - EV) be most appropriate?
options: When future performance is expected to return to plan
When the project is already complete
questions.explanation: Use this when current variance is believed to be atypical and will not continue.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of TCPI?
options: To show the CPI required on remaining work to meet a goal
To replace CPI in all calculations
questions.explanation: TCPI indicates the efficiency needed on the remaining work.

questions.question: Which statement about BAC is correct?
options: BAC is the actual cost to date
BAC is the forecasted final cost
BAC is the total approved project budget
BAC is the earned value of completed work
questions.explanation: BAC is the total overall project budget.

questions.question: Which metric is most useful to determine if a project is financially efficient right now?
questions.explanation: CPI measures cost efficiency at the current point in time.

questions.question: Which metric is most useful to determine if a project is progressing on time right now?
questions.explanation: SV directly shows whether the project is ahead or behind schedule.

questions.question: Which metric is best described as a ratio of earned value to planned value?
questions.explanation: SPI compares earned value to planned value.

questions.question: Which metric is best described as a ratio of earned value to actual cost?
questions.explanation: CPI compares earned value to actual cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three core EVA input metrics?
questions.explanation: SPI is a derived metric, not a foundational input.

questions.question: Which of the following is a forecast metric rather than a current status metric?
questions.explanation: EAC is used to forecast final cost.

questions.question: What does a TCPI value above 1 generally signal?
options: The project can finish with less effort than planned
The remaining work must be done more efficiently than before
The project is guaranteed to be ahead of schedule
questions.explanation: TCPI > 1 means the remaining work needs higher efficiency to achieve the target.

questions.question: Why is EVA especially useful for large or complex projects?
options: It removes the need for budgeting
It provides objective integrated control over schedule and cost
It works only for small projects
questions.explanation: EVA is most valuable when both time and cost must be tracked objectively.

questions.question: For which type of project may EVA be overkill?
questions.explanation: Very small, short projects often do not justify the overhead of EVA.

questions.question: Which statement best explains the relationship among PV, EV, and AC?
options: PV shows what was spent, EV shows what was planned, AC shows what was earned
PV shows planned work value, EV shows completed work value, AC shows actual spending
PV, EV, and AC are all the same metric
AC is always equal to EV
questions.explanation: These three metrics represent planned value, earned value, and actual spending respectively.

questions.question: If SPI is 0.80, what is the correct interpretation?
questions.explanation: SPI below 1 means behind schedule; 0.80 indicates about 20% behind.

questions.question: If CPI is 0.84, what is the correct interpretation?
questions.explanation: CPI below 1 means over budget; 0.84 indicates about 16% over budget.

questions.question: Which metric indicates the amount of work value earned relative to budget spent?
questions.explanation: CPI compares earned value with actual cost, showing cost efficiency.

questions.question: Which metric indicates the amount of work value earned relative to planned work?
questions.explanation: SPI compares earned value to planned value and reflects schedule efficiency.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about absolute and relative metrics?
options: Absolute metrics are ratios; relative metrics are dollars
Absolute metrics show magnitude; relative metrics show efficiency
Absolute metrics are only for forecasting
Relative metrics cannot be compared across projects
questions.explanation: Variance metrics show dollar magnitude, while indices show relative performance.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate use of variance metrics such as SV and CV?
options: Comparing projects of very different sizes only
Understanding exact dollar deviations from plan
questions.explanation: Variance metrics are useful for understanding the exact dollar gap from plan.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate use of index metrics such as SPI and CPI?
questions.explanation: Indices are normalized ratios that help compare performance across projects.

questions.question: Which metric is directly used to identify whether a project is over or under budget at the current point in time?
questions.explanation: CV directly indicates whether the project is currently over or under budget.

questions.question: Which metric is directly used to identify whether a project is ahead or behind schedule at the current point in time?
questions.explanation: SV directly indicates whether the project is currently ahead or behind schedule.

questions.question: Which forecast metric tells you how much more money must be spent from now until completion?
questions.explanation: ETC is the remaining amount needed to finish the project.

questions.question: Which forecast metric tells you whether the final project cost is expected to be above or below budget?
questions.explanation: VAC compares BAC and EAC to show surplus or deficit at completion.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid interpretation of EV > AC?
options: The project is getting good value for money
The project is behind schedule automatically
The project has no budget risk
questions.explanation: When EV exceeds AC, the project has earned more value than it spent.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid interpretation of EV < PV?
questions.explanation: EV below PV means less work was completed than planned.

questions.question: In EVA, why is a project manager interested in both current status and forecast metrics?
options: Because current metrics show history, while forecast metrics project the future
Because forecast metrics are only for schedule
Because current metrics are only for cost
questions.explanation: Current status explains what has happened; forecasts estimate what will happen.

questions.question: Which formula shows the remaining cost assuming the project continues at the same performance level?
questions.explanation: ETC is the difference between forecast final cost and cost spent to date.

questions.question: Which formula is most directly associated with the idea of finishing the project on budget?
questions.explanation: TCPI estimates the efficiency needed on remaining work to meet the original budget.

questions.question: A project can have a CPI greater than 1 and an SPI less than 1. What does that indicate?
options: It is ahead of schedule and over budget
It is under budget but behind schedule
It is over budget and ahead of schedule
It is on budget and on schedule
questions.explanation: CPI > 1 means under budget, while SPI < 1 means behind schedule.
